questions.question: A person covers a distance of 7.5 km at a speed of 25 m/sec. What is the time taken by the person to cover the mentioned distance?
questions.solution:
Given:

A person covers a distance of 7.5 km at a speed of 25 m/sec.

Concept used:

1. 1 km = 1000m

2. Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

7.5 km = 7500 metres

Now, the time taken by the person to cover the mentioned distance

⇒ 7500/25

⇒ 300 seconds

⇒ 300/60 minutes

⇒ 5 minutes

**∴ The time taken by the person to cover the mentioned distance is 5 minutes.**

questions.question: A car covers 60 km at a speed of 84 km/h. If the average speed for the whole journey is 72 km/h, then the speed of the car for the next 60 km of the journey is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered in the first part = 60 km at a speed of 84 km/h.

Distance covered in the second part = 60 km.

Average speed for the whole journey = 72 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken to cover the first 60 km = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time taken for the first 60 km = 60 / 84 hours

Total distance for the whole journey = 60 + 60 = 120 km

Given average speed for the whole journey = 72 km/h

Total time for the whole journey = Total distance / Average speed

⇒ Total time for 120 km = 120 / 72 hours

Let the speed for the next 60 km be x km/h.

Time taken for the next 60 km = 60 / x hours

According to the given information:

Total time = Time for first 60 km + Time for next 60 km

⇒ 120 / 72 = (60 / 84) + (60 / x)

Solving for x:

⇒ 5 / 3 = (5 / 7) + (60 / x)

⇒ 60 / x = (5 / 3) - (5 / 7)

⇒ 60 / x = (35 - 15) / 21

⇒ 60 / x = 20 / 21

⇒ x = (60 × 21) / 20

⇒ x = 63 km/h

**The speed of the car for the next 60 km of the journey is 63 km/h.**

questions.question: A 750 metres long train crosses a stationary pole in 15 sec. Travelling at the same speed, this train crosses a bridge completely in 25 sec. What is the length of this bridge?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of time taken = 15 : 25 = 3 : 5.

Since speed is constant, distance ratio = time ratio = 3 : 5.

Distance while crossing pole = Train length = 3 units = 750 m.

⇒ 1 unit = 250 m.

Distance while crossing bridge = (Train + Bridge) = 5 units.

Bridge length = (5 − 3) units = 2 units = 2 × 250 = 500 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 500 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train = 750 m

Time to cross pole = 15 sec

Time to cross bridge = 25 sec

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance when crossing a bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge

 
• 
 
 Train
 
• 
 Pole
 Case 1: 750m in 15s
 
 
• 
 
 
 Train
 Bridge (L)
 Case 2: (750 + L)m in 25s
 
 Total = 25s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of train = Length of train ÷ Time taken to cross pole

⇒ Speed = 750 ÷ 15

⇒ Speed = 50 m/sec

⇒ While crossing the bridge, Total distance = Speed × Time taken

⇒ 750 + Length of bridge = 50 × 25

⇒ 750 + Length of bridge = 1250

⇒ Length of bridge = 1250 − 750

⇒ Length of bridge = 500 m

**∴ The correct answer is 500 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Distance Rule

When a train crosses a stationary point object (pole, man), distance = Train length. For a platform or bridge, distance = Train length + Bridge length.

Relative Speed

If two trains of lengths L₁ and L₂ cross each other, total distance is always (L₁ + L₂) regardless of direction.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A cyclist covers a distance of 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover a distance of 12 km at the same speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the cyclist = 2.5 km

Time taken to cover 2.5 km = 4 minutes 10 seconds = 4 × 60 + 10 = 250 seconds

Distance to be covered = 12 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed of the cyclist = 2.5 / 250 km/s

⇒ Speed = 0.01 km/s

The time taken to cover 12 km

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 12 / 0.01 seconds

⇒ Time = 1200 seconds

Time = 1200 / 60 minutes

⇒ Time = 20 minutes

**The cyclist will take 20 minutes to cover 12 km at the same speed.**

questions.question: Neha walks at the rate of 8 km/h and crosses a bridge in 27 minutes. What is the length of the bridge in metres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Neha = 8 km/h.

Time taken to cross the bridge = 27 minutes = 27/60 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Time = 27/60 hours = 0.45 hours

Distance (Length of the bridge) = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 8 km/h × 0.45 h

⇒ Distance = 3.6 km

⇒ Distance in metres = 3.6 × 1000 = 3600 metres

**The length of the bridge is 3600 metres.**

questions.question: If Mohan travels with 60 percent speed of his usual speed, then he will reach 10 minutes late. What is the usual time taken by him?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New speed = 60% = 3/5 of usual speed.

If speed becomes a/b of usual speed, Usual Time = [a / (b − a)] × Late Time

Here, a = 3, b = 5, Late Time = 10 minutes.

Usual Time = [3 / (5 − 3)] × 10

Usual Time = (3 / 2) × 10 = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Let the usual speed be S and usual time be T minutes.

Distance remains constant in both cases. Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9e16a9d605a261afbc789391f4de3166542704330c1ae25742d7437bdf832c6.png] 

⇒ Usual Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = 60% of S = 0.6S

⇒ New Time = (T + 10) minutes

⇒ New Distance = 0.6S × (T + 10)

Equating both distances:

⇒ S × T = 0.6S × (T + 10)

⇒ T = 0.6T + 6

⇒ T − 0.6T = 6

⇒ 0.4T = 6

⇒ T = 6 ÷ 0.4 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T). Therefore, Speed Ratio = Inverse of Time Ratio.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |a − b|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = a + b.
</p

questions.question: A girl goes from A to B with speed 60 km/hr and return from B to A with speed 30 km/hr. If whole journey takes 5 hours, then what is the distance between A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a person travels a certain distance at speed S₁ and returns at speed S₂ taking total time T, the distance is given by:

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂) ] × Total Time

Distance = [ (60 × 30) ÷ (60 + 30) ] × 5

Distance = [ 1800 ÷ 90 ] × 5 = 20 × 5 = 100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 60 km/hr

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 30 km/hr

Total time taken (T) = 5 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db13c818c5460bd7700857e1bfe0a86e1e29c2019966f1744c3f965a2e2612bd.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the total distance between A and B be D km.

⇒ Time taken to travel from A to B = D ÷ 60 hours

⇒ Time taken to return from B to A = D ÷ 30 hours

The total time for the whole journey is given as 5 hours.

⇒ (D ÷ 60) + (D ÷ 30) = 5

⇒ (D + 2D) ÷ 60 = 5

⇒ 3D ÷ 60 = 5

⇒ D ÷ 20 = 5

⇒ D = 20 × 5

⇒ D = 100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When an object covers two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the entire journey is calculated as (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

When an object travels at speed S₁ for a certain time and at speed S₂ for an equal amount of time, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

If two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they are moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).
</p
